rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted predicate is that the matter is as God wills; the phrase urges acknowledgment that He may preserve or ruin the garden and all it contains.
rows.anchor: ما موصولة خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying there is no power except through God admits human incapacity and that cultivating and managing the garden depended on divine aid and enabling.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بعجزك وبأن ما تيسر لك من عمارتها وتدبيرها

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A report says that one who admires something and says this remembrance will be protected from the evil eye.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من رأى شيئا فأعجبه فقال : ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله لم تضره العين"

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A report says that someone who sees another granted family or wealth and says this remembrance will see no harm in it.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من رأى أحدا أعطي خيرا من أهل أو مال فقال عنده ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله لم ير فيه مكروها"

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet explains that avoiding disobedience requires God's protection, while strength to obey comes only from Him.
rows.anchor: وفسر النبي عليه السلام معنى لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله فقال : "لا حول تحول عن معاصي الله إلا بعصمة الله

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: A report calls this remembrance a remedy for ninety-nine ailments, the least of them worry.
rows.anchor: وروي "أنها دواء من تسعة وتسعين داء أيسرها الهم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original wording is أن ترني; أقل is either a circumstantial accusative with visual seeing or the second object of cognitive seeing, and أنا reinforces the omitted first-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: أصله أن ترني والرؤية إما بصرية بأقل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden's water may sink into the earth beyond reach of hands or buckets; the verbal noun غورا intensifies the description.
rows.anchor: غائرا في الأرض ذاهبا لا تناله الأيدي ولا الدلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one would be able even to search for the vanished water, much less find and restore it.
rows.anchor: فضلا عن وجدانه ورده

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn says the water would leave no trace by which it could be sought.
rows.anchor: قال في الجلالين لا يبقى له أثر تطلبه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened disaster occurs: the two gardens and all their contents are destroyed; being surrounded by an enemy conveys being overcome and ruined.
rows.anchor: مأخوذ من أحاط به العدو لأنه إذا أحاط به فقد غلبه واستولى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning the palms over expresses regret and grief, as a regretful person commonly strikes one hand against the other.
rows.anchor: ظهرا لبطن تأسفا وتحسرا كما هو عادة النادمين

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: The gestures of turning the palms, biting the hand or fingertips, and gnashing the teeth are metonymies for regret because they accompany it.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" تقليب الكفين وعض الكف والأنامل

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: A cited couplet says that grieving over what has passed is wrong because what is gone will not return and remembering it is futile.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His regret is expressed over the money spent cultivating the garden; sorrow over voluntary spending can stand for sorrow over the garden obtained with it.
rows.anchor: ولعل تخصيص الندم به دون ما هلك الآن من الجنة لما أنه إنما يكون على الأفعال الاختيارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grape garden is empty and collapsed: its vine supports fell, and the vines fell over them; it is singled out as the principal asset.
rows.anchor: أي : الجنة من الأعناب المحفوفة بنخل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says God sent fire that burned the garden and its water sank away.
rows.anchor: قيل أرسل الله عليها نارا فأحرقتها وغار ماؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner recalls his brother's admonition and realizes that associating partners with God caused his ruin; wishing for faith now is not sincere repentance because he wanted faith for worldly gain.
rows.anchor: كأنه تذكر موعظة أخيه وعلم أنه إنما أتي من جهة الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brother's admonition failed because the listener's heart had become harder, so his outcome was regret.
rows.anchor: ألا يرى لم ينجع فيه وعظ أخيه المسلم لزيادة قسوة قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly-life parable should show its beauty, freshness, and swift disappearance so people do not rely on it or abandon the afterlife.
rows.anchor: اذكر لقومك وبين ما يشبهها في زهرتها ونضارتها وسرعة زوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is explained as the world being like water; heaven here can mean a cloud or the direction of the sky.
rows.anchor: استئناف لبيان المثل أي : هي كمآء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison concerns the whole sequence within the simile, not water by itself.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد تشبيه حال الدنيا بالماء وحده بل بمجموع ما في حيز الأداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's plants intertwine and grow dense from the water, making the land fresh and flourishing.
rows.anchor: وتكاثف بسببه حتى خالط بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هشيما means the vegetation has become dry, crushed, and broken; the root refers to breaking something soft.
rows.anchor: مهشوما مكسورا ليبسه من الهشم وهو كسر الشيء الرخو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds carry the broken plants away and scatter them; the lexicon also uses the verb for winnowing grain in wind.
rows.anchor: تحمله وتفرقه يقال ذرت الريح الشيء وأذرته وذرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse condenses the fuller parable of worldly life in Yunus.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مختصرة من قوله : {إنما مثل الحيواة الدنيا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi compares human youth and freshness to a flourishing tree that death dries out, while hopes and desires are blown into nothingness.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (همنين آدمى بزندكى وتازكى كه دارد خوش برآيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has complete power over creating, preserving, and annihilating everything.
rows.anchor: من الإنشاء والإبقاء والإفناء وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person should not be deceived by worldly life: it perishes even when long-lasting and vanishes despite its adornment.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن لا يغتر بالحياة الدنيا فإنها فانية ولو طالت مدتها

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saadi's examples of aging, a king's silk shroud eaten by worms, and renewed spring warn that life passes while the world continues.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an inward allegory, primordial care joins spirit to body as water joins earth; prophets and saints sow faith and monotheism through invitation in the heart's fertile soil, nourished by the Law.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الذي أدركته العناية الأزلية بعد تعلق الروح بالجسد كتعلق الماء بالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seed of monotheism grows into faith, raising the spirit from low human nature toward spiritual ranks and divine nearness through the good word and righteous action.
rows.anchor: فينبت عن بذر التوحيد وهي كلمة لا إله إلا الله شجرة الإيمان بماء الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may abandon the spirit to animal-like corporeality or draw it by grace to the highest nearness, where even the angels prostrate to it.
rows.anchor: قادر على أن يخذله وينفيه في أسفل سافلين الجسمانية الحيوانية

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami says seekers cannot arrive through years of effort alone without the beloved's attraction.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الجامي : سالكان بى كشش دوست بجايى نرسند

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says an account in a book calls worldly life a gain for the discerning and heedlessness for the ignorant; prophets and saints lived in it without attachment.
rows.anchor: قال وهب : رأيت في بعض الكتب الدنيا غنيمة الأكياس وغفلة الجهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet, together with the believers who follow him, is commanded to tell the unbelievers about the greatest losers in deeds.
rows.anchor: نخبركم أنا ومن تبعني من المؤمنين أيها الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخسرين أعمالا is an accusative of specification; its plural signals varied kinds of deeds and means the greatest loss among creatures.
rows.anchor: نصب على التمييز والجمع للإيذان بتنوعها

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad reads this as unbelievers whose deeds were good in themselves, such as charity and freeing slaves, and who proudly expected reward from them.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : هذا بيان حال الكفرة باعتبار ما صدر عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their efforts to establish intrinsically good works are entirely wasted; the loss of their effort is not limited to worldly life.
rows.anchor: في إقامة الأعمال الحسنة في أنفسها أي : ضاع وبطل بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imagine their efforts will benefit them in the afterlife because they admire the works they struggled to perform and think they did them properly.
rows.anchor: يعني : يعملون عملا ينفعهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward warning includes innovators, people seeking reputation, and the ostentatious: even slight ostentation is hidden shirk that cancels deeds.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أهل الأهواء والبدع وأهل الرياء والسمعة فإن اليسير من الرياء شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds alongside disbelief or hidden association are rejected; this also warns against people seeking thanks from others and monks who impose harsh retreats while imagining they worship rightly.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان ما هو طاعة مردودا لمجاورته المنافي فما ظنك بما هو معصية في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers and those doing righteous deeds unite inward work of the heart with outward work of the limbs.
rows.anchor: جمعوا بين عمل القلب وعمل الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will create affection for them in people's hearts without their needing kinship, friendship, favors, or other usual causes; this may be after Islam gains strength or on Judgment Day through their displayed good deeds.
rows.anchor: سيحدث لهم في القلوب مودة من غير تعرض منهم لأسبابها من قرابة أو صداقة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The faith-seed in the heart, nourished by righteous deeds, grows to bear love of God, the prophets, angels, and believers.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن بذر الإيمان إذا وقع في أرض القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affection progresses from natural accord to inclination, heart-level fondness, inward love, overpowering passion, and ecstatic excess.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المحبة الموافقة ثم الميل ثم الود ثم الهوى ثم الوله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن جعفر
rows.claim: Asked how to know whether a man's claim of love is true, he advises testing one's heart: if it feels affection for him, he loves you.
rows.anchor: قال رجل لعبد الله بن جعفر : إن فلانا يقول أنا أحبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited couplet says hearts reveal one another's affection before the bodies are seen.
rows.anchor: وعلى القلوب من القلوب دلائل بالود قبل تشاهد الأشباح

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A report urges increasing the number of brothers, saying God's generosity would make Him ashamed to punish His servant among them on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أكثروا من الاخوان فإن ربكم حي كريم يستحيى أن يعذب عبده بين اخوانه يوم القيامة"

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet says that looking affectionately at a brother without malice brings forgiveness for prior sins before the next blink.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : "من نظر إلى أخيه نظر مودة ولم يكن في قلبه إحن

rows.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Umar says greeting first, making room, and using a brother's favorite name establish affection in his heart.
rows.anchor: ثلاث يثبتن الود في صدر أخيك أن تبدأه بالسلام وأن توسع له

rows.speaker: سقراط
rows.claim: Socrates says praising an affectionate person before others sustains fondness, while a bad reputation fuels enmity.
rows.anchor: وقال سقراط اثن على ذي المودة خيرا عند من لقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since delayed punishment is respite rather than neglect and will certainly come, the Prophet should endure their accusations of disbelief, sorcery, and madness until judgment; certainty of their punishment consoles him.
rows.anchor: فاصبر على ما يقولون فيك من كلمات الكفر والنسبة إلى السحر والجنون

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The objections and denials are part of the Prophet's spiritual training toward the station of patience.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" على ما يقول أهل الاعتراض والإنكار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say this command to endure was abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : هذا منسوخ بآية السيف

rows.speaker: الكبير
rows.claim: Al-Kabir says abrogation is unnecessary because the Prophet could fight and still endure their verbal abuse.
rows.anchor: وفي "الكبير" هذا غير لازم لجواز أن يقاتل ويصبر على ما يسمع منهم من الأذى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines patience as restraining oneself for what reason and law require or from what they forbid; its name varies by setting, such as courage in battle, broadness of chest in calamity, and concealment in silence.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الصبر حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih with praise means prayer, using a part for the whole; remembrance soothes the heart and makes grief recede.
rows.anchor: أي : صل حامدا لربك على هدايته وتوفيقه

rows.speaker: الخبر
rows.claim: A report says remembrance and glorification until sunrise surpass freeing eighty descendants of Ishmael; he is singled out for his nobility and as ancestor of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر "إن الذكر والتسبيح إلى طلوع الشمس أفضل من إعتاق ثمانين رقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before sunrise means the dawn prayer; before sunset means the noon and afternoon prayers, both after the sun passes its zenith.
rows.anchor: المراد صلاة الفجر وفي الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night prayers are Maghrib and Isha; they are especially virtuous because the heart is more collected and the self inclines to rest, making worship harder.
rows.anchor: فصل والمراد المغرب والعشاء وتقديم الوقت فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أطراف النهار directs voluntary prayers during the parts of daytime.
rows.anchor: {وأطراف النهار} أمر بالتطوع أجزاء النهار

rows.speaker: العيون
rows.claim: Al-Uyun reads the phrase in the accusative with the preceding time expressions and identifies the prayers as Maghrib and repeated Fajr for emphasis; some exegetes instead identify Asr.
rows.anchor: وفي "العيون" هو بالنصب عطف على ما قبله من الظروف

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn identifies before sunset as Asr and the daytime edges as Dhuhr in the second half of the day.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" قبل غروبها صلاة العصر وأطراف النهار صلاة الظهر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies before sunset as Asr, night as Isha, and the daytime edges as Dhuhr and Maghrib; Dhuhr touches both halves and Maghrib closes the second.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري قبل غروبها وهي العصر ومن آناء الليل هي العشاء الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم الفزاري
rows.claim: Al-Fazari cites this interpretation and notes related discussion at the ends of Hud and in Qaf.
rows.anchor: وبهذا احتج الشيخ أبو القاسم الفزاري في "الأسئلة المقحمة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لعلك ترضى attaches to tasbih: worship at these times in hope that God grants contentment and gladdens the heart.
rows.anchor: أي : سبح في هذه الأوقات رجاء أن تنال عنده تعالى ما ترضى به نفسك

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the most likely promised honor that satisfies the Prophet is intercession for his community, supported by the promise that his Lord will give until he is content.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (خوشنودى در اصح اقوال بكرامتى ماشدكه خداى تعالى اورا عطا دهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih is seeking support against deniers; prayer is the strongest remedy for pain, the Prophet turned to it when distressed, and this verse gathers the five prayers.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الاشتغال بالتسبيح استنصار من المسبح للنصر على المكذبين وأن الصلاة أعظم ترياق

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jarir reports the Prophet compared the believers' vision of God to seeing the full moon and urged guarding the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
rows.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرأى القمر ليلة البدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with a doubled mīm derives from mutual crowding: people will not crowd or press one another to see; a tāʾ is omitted from the original form.
rows.anchor: بتشديد الميم من الضم أي : لا يضم بعضكم بعضا ولا يقول أرنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate light-mīm reading derives from injustice: no one will be excluded from the vision, and all share equally in it.
rows.anchor: وروى بتخفيف الميم من الضيم وهو الظلم فالتاء مضمومة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A hadith says Isha and Fajr are the heaviest prayers for hypocrites, who would attend even crawling if they knew their reward.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن أثقل الصلاة على المنافقين صلاة العشاء والفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report promises broad spiritual and worldly benefits for keeping the five prayers in congregation and severe losses for treating them lightly.
rows.anchor: يقال : من داوم على الصلوات الخمس في الجماعة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A hadith calls the Muslim community one shown mercy and says God averts calamities through their sincerity, prayers, supplication, and weak members.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أمتي أمة مرحومة" وإنما يدفع الله عنهم البلايا بإخلاصهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that Daniel said a people praying the prayer of Muhammad's community would have spared Noah's people from drowning, Ad from the wind, and Thamud from the blast.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة أن دانيال النبي عليه السلام نعت أمة محمد فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer should remain constant in prayer, supplication, and seeking refuge with God.
rows.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن لا ينفك عن الصلاة والدعاء والالتجاء إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مد means stretching or extending, and its noun مدة denotes an extended period; إمداد is often used for desirable things, while مد often appears with harm.
rows.anchor: أصل المد الجر ومنه المدة للوقت الممتد وأكثر ما جاء الإمداد في المحبوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eye is the physical organ, unlike sight; the sacred report says God is the servant's hearing and sight, not ear and eye. The command means not to gaze with desire and inclination.
rows.anchor: الحديث القدسي "كنت له سمعا وبصرا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage identifies Abu Jahl as one who disputes about God without necessary knowledge, sound reasoning, or revealed proof, relying only on blind imitation and thereby displaying extreme ignorance.
rows.anchor: هو أبو جهل {يجادل فى الله} حال كون ذلك المجادل

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh defines the side as the part a person bends or inclines when turning away from something; folding it signals arrogance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ العطف بكسر العين الجانب الذي يعطفه الإنسان ويلويه

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn explains turning one's side as turning the neck in pride.
rows.anchor: ففي الجلالين لاوي عنقه تكبرا

rows.speaker: التفسير الفارسي
rows.claim: The Persian commentary takes the phrase as a metaphor for arrogance: the person draws away his garment's side from everything.
rows.anchor: وفي "التفسير الفارسي" : (ييدة دامن خوداست واين كنايه

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad describes him as arrogantly turning his side, folding his flank, and turning away.
rows.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" : عاطفا بجانبه وطاويا كشحه معرضا متكبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of his disputation is to lead people away from God's path, whether by turning believers from guidance or keeping unbelievers in error.
rows.anchor: متعلق بيجادل فإن غرضه الإضلال عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility increases affection, forbearance brings supporters, gentleness wins hearts, fidelity sustains brotherhood, and truthfulness completes virtue; the prayer asks release from base traits and acquisition of good qualities.
rows.anchor: وبالتواضع تكثر المحبة. وبالحلم تكثر الأنصار.

rows.speaker: الرواة
rows.claim: The verse is reported to concern Bedouins who settled in Medina when healthy, prosperous, and blessed with children, but called the religion bad fortune when hardship came and turned away.
rows.anchor: روي : أن الآية نزلت في أعاريب قدموا المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping on an edge means standing at the religion's margin without inward roots, like a soldier who stays only while victory seems likely and otherwise flees.
rows.anchor: على طرف من الدين لا في وسطه وقلبه فلا ثبات له فيه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says alphabet letters are the edges of a word joined to one another.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : حروف الهجاء أطراف الكلمة الرابطة بعضها ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here good means worldly health and abundance; such a person settles outwardly in religion because of that good, without the inner assurance of steadfast believers.
rows.anchor: أي دنيوي من الصحة والسعة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the phrase as becoming settled and firm in religion because of that worldly favor.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي (آرام كير بدين وثابت شود برآن بسبب آن يز)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trial means an unwelcome event affecting one's self, family, or wealth; good is also a trial, and hardship is not evil in itself because patient acceptance can bring nearness and rank.
rows.anchor: شيء يفتن به من مكروه يعتريه في نفسه أو أهله أو ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning back on one's face means abandoning the direction and path of Islam and returning to disbelief.
rows.anchor: الانقلاب الانصراف والرجوع والوجه بمعنى الجهة والطريقة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi paraphrases the phrase as returning along the way one came, meaning apostasy and leaving Islam.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (بركردد برروي خود يعني ازجهتي كه آمده

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Bahr says that على can mean عن, turning away from the direction of faith, as in the verse about God's provision for every creature.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : قوله في "بحر العلوم" : تحول عن وجهه فانكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearer reading is worldly loss through losing one's family in hardship and afterlife loss through forfeiting reward after abandoning religion and entering Hell.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن خسران الدنيا ذهاب أهله حيث أصابته فتنة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says worldly loss is failing to reach one's aim, while afterlife loss is the destruction of one's deeds after losing religion.
rows.anchor: كما قال الكاشفي : (زيان كرد دنيا كه بمراد نرسد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view defines worldly loss as abandoning obedience and persisting in disobedience, and afterlife loss as numerous adversaries and liabilities.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الخسران في الدنيا ترك الطاعات ولزوم المخالفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The introductory حتى begins a sentence but also marks the endpoint of the preceding account: the unbelievers persist in false claims until death, when the afterlife becomes visible.
rows.anchor: حتى التي يبتدأ بها الكلام دخلت على الجملة الاسمية وهي مع ذلك غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At irreversible death, the unbeliever regrets neglecting faith and deeds and begs to be returned.
rows.anchor: تحسرا على ما فرط فيه من الإيمان والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural waw in ارجعون honors a singular addressee; the author rejects the claim that such honorific plural address occurs only in later Arabic.
rows.anchor: والواو لتعظيم المخاطب لأن العرب تخاطب الواحد الجليل الشأن بلفظ الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He imagines being asked whether he wants to return to gather wealth, plant, build, or dig canals, then says he wants to do righteous work with the faith he left behind.
rows.anchor: إلى أي شيء تذهب إلى جمع المال أو غرس الغراس أو بناء البنيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not frame faith itself as a hope because he presents it as definite, while righteous action is what he hopes to perform.
rows.anchor: فلم ينظم الإيمان في سلك الرجاء كسائر الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn interprets the hoped-for righteous work as testifying to God's oneness, which he left undone in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال في "الجلالين" : {لعلي أعمل صالحا} أي أشهد بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view addresses the Angel of Death and his helpers; the mention of Lord is an oath, and the man appeals first to God and then to the angels.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الخطاب في ارجعون لملك الموت وأعوانه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says a believer who sees the angels declines return to the world and welcomes going to God, whereas an unbeliever asks to be returned.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه قوله عليه السلام : "إذا عاين المؤمن الملائكة قالوا : أنرجعك إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: الكبير
rows.claim: Al-Kabir considers فيما تركت broader: it includes neglected worship and both bodily and financial duties or rights.
rows.anchor: قال في "الكبير" : وهو أقرب كأنهم تمنوا الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barzakh lasts until resurrection and wholly rules out returning to worldly life; the return at resurrection is to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهو إقناط كلي من الرجعة إلى الدنيا لما علم أن لا رجعة يوم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet blast is the second one that raises the dead; the horn-like trumpet is a means God uses to return souls to their bodies.
rows.anchor: لقيام الساعة وهي النفخة الثانية التي عندها البعث والنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship will not benefit them, either because panic erases tenderness and makes relatives flee one another or because there will be no lineage to boast about; lineage is shared parentage, vertically or among collateral relatives.
rows.anchor: تنفعهم لزوال التراحم والتعاطف من فرط واستيلاء الدهشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will not ask one another's identity or tribe because each is absorbed in himself by terror and cannot recognize others.
rows.anchor: {ولا يتسآءلون} أي لا يسأل بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not contradict people later questioning one another: the lack of questions is at the onset of the second blast before reckoning, or during stations when terror overwhelms them; later they recover and converse.
rows.anchor: ولا يناقضه قوله تعالى : {فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتسآءلون}

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report from Aisha, the Prophet says there are three places where everyone is distracted: when books are delivered, at the scales, and on the bridge over Hell.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : يا رسول الله أما نتعارف

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says each servant will be publicly named and creditors invited to claim their due; people will rejoice if a right is established against even a close relative.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : يؤخذ بيد العبد والأمة يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In an inward reading, divine care breathed into the heart raises its spiritual resurrection: worldly ties fall away as each person seeks God, absorbed in love and unconcerned with family, companions, or homeland.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن نفخة العناية الربوبية إذا نفخت في صور القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighed things are sound beliefs and righteous deeds, which have worth and weight with God.
rows.anchor: موزونات حسناته من العقائد والأعمال أي فمن كان له عقائد صحيحة وأعمال صالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful attain every desired thing and escape every feared thing; the wording shifts from singular by grammatical form to plural by meaning.
rows.anchor: الفائزون بكل مطلوب الناجون من كل مهروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with light scales lack beliefs and deeds that have worth before God; they are unbelievers, as the verse about giving them no weight says.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يكن له من العقائد والأعمال ماله وزن وقدر عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose themselves by wasting the time needed to complete their potential; خسران means a shortfall in one's capital.
rows.anchor: ضيعوها بتضييع زمان استكمالها وأبطلوا استعدادها لنيل كمالها

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says they squandered life's capital in heedlessness and wasted their capacity for perfection by pursuing desires and following appetites.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي (س كروه آنندكه زيان كرده اند ازنفسهاي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Tawilat compares a person to an egg whose potential becomes a chick through the hen's care; once that potential is altered and care ends, it cannot be restored. A mystic who abandons the path is worse off than one abandoning the legal religion.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : الإنسان كالبيضة المستعدة لقبول تصرف ولاية الدجاجة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The altered spiritual nature explains remaining in Hell: the ruined potential cannot be brought back to its former state.
rows.anchor: أي في جهنم أنفسهم فلا يخرجون بالفروخية وليس من سنة الله إصلاح الاستعداد

rows.speaker: الجامي
rows.claim: Jami's couplet says that one swallowed by the earth cannot be brought out even by Moses and Aaron, and no healer can repair the reversal of fate.
rows.anchor: قال الجامي : آنراكه زمين كشد درون ون قارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is the world they ask to return to; لبث means staying continuously in a place, and عدد سنين specifies the number of years.
rows.anchor: التي تدعون أن ترجعوا إليها يقال لبث بالمكان أقام به ملازما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say a day or part of one because worldly life seems brief beside Hell's duration, because pleasurable days pass quickly, or because what is over is like nothing.
rows.anchor: استقصارا لمدة لبثهم فيها بالنسبة إلى دخولهم في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who could count their time say torment now occupies them so fully that they cannot remember or calculate it.
rows.anchor: أي الذين يعلمون عد أيامها إن أردت تحقيقها فإنا لما نحن فيه من العذاب مشغولون

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading takes the counters as the angels assigned to record people's breaths, days, and nights.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : فاسأل العادين يعني الذين يعدون أنفاسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God confirms that the stay was little; grammatically, قليلا describes an omitted stay or period of time.
rows.anchor: تصديقا لهم في تقليلهم لسني لبثهم في الدنيا وقليلا صفة مصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Bahr says that if they had known how long their worldly stay was, they would have answered differently; the lesson is to repair deeds before breath and life end.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : أي لو كنتم تعلمون مقدار لبثكم من الطول

rows.speaker: أردشير بن بابك
rows.claim: Ardashir says not to rely on the world because it lasts for no one, yet not to abandon it because the afterlife is attained through it.
rows.anchor: قال أردشير بن بابك بن ساسان وهو أول ملك من آل ساسان : لا تركنن إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari urges making use of the remaining breath and chance to act, and dropping excuses while one's term is limited.
rows.anchor: قال العلامة الزمخشري استغنم تنفس الأجل وإمكان العمل

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saadi's verses urge sowing while it is time, valuing each precious breath, and not wasting one's life in regret because time is a sword.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره : كنون وقت تخمست اكر روري

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The cited inward interpretation says God knows what creatures do completely, while creatures know according to their capacities; this does not exclude God enabling objects or animals to speak miraculously or in ways perceived only by people of unveiling.
rows.anchor: أي : بحقيقته بالكمال وهم يعلمون بحسب استعدادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prays to be among those whose breaths pass in remembrance and whose time passes in a gentle spiritual state.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله سبحانه وتعالى أن يجعلنا ممن لا يمضي نفسه إلا بذكر شريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يزجي means gently and easily driving something along, especially an insignificant thing; this hints that clouds are negligible relative to God's power. Clouds are named for their movement through air, and here the plural parts are intended.
rows.anchor: الإزجاء سوق الشيء برفق وسهولة لينساق غلب في سوق شيء يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes seeing God visually guide clouds wherever He wills.
rows.anchor: والمعنى قد رأيت رؤية بصرية أن الله يسوق غيما إلى حيث يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God joins separate cloud portions into one, then piles them on top of one another; ركام means a gathered mass.
rows.anchor: بين أجزائه بضم بعضها إلى بعض فيجعله شيئا واحدا بعد أن كان قطعا

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth defines الودق as all rain, whether heavy or light.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث : الودق المطر كله شديده وهينه

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat reports an alternative definition of الودق as the dust-like material visible among raindrops, also used for rain itself.
rows.anchor: وفي "المفردات" : الودق قيل ما يكون خلال المطر كأنه غبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gap phrase is circumstantial with visual seeing; cloud openings are the spaces between things and here are passages through which drops emerge.
rows.anchor: حال من الودق لأن الرؤية بصرية والخلال جمع خلل كجبال وجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain comes out from the cloud's gaps and openings created by the accumulation and compression of its parts.
rows.anchor: حال كون ذلك الودق يخرج من أثناء ذلك السحاب وفتوقه التي حدثت بالتراكم

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says clouds act as a sieve for rain; without them rain would ruin what it struck.
rows.anchor: قال كعب : السحاب غربال المطر ولولاه لأفسد المطر ما يقع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here السماء means the clouds, since anything above you is called sky, and the sky is the highest part of anything.
rows.anchor: أي من الغمام فإن كل ما علاك سماء وسماء كل شيء أعلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hail comes from immense chunks resembling mountains, located in the sky; sky is grammatically feminine here.
rows.anchor: {من جبال} أي : من قطع عظام تشبه الجبال في العظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من before hail marks the object as partitive, while the earlier instances mark source and the second is an appositive relation; hail is frozen water.
rows.anchor: مفعول ينزل على أن من تبعيضية والأوليان لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says God made mountains of ice and snow in the sky and assigned an angel to release measured hail or snow onto a region by His command.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن الله تعالى خلق جبالا كثيرة في السماء من البرد والثلج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every spring running on earth ultimately comes from snow and ice.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا عين تجري على الأرض إلا وأصلها من البرد والثلج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says angels are half ice and half fire; by flapping their wings they send down the snow that falls from them.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إن الله تعالى خلق ملائكة نصف أبدانهم من الثلج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the sky as the encompassing celestial sphere containing mountains of hail, like the stone mountains on earth; reason does not rule it out.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد من الماء أي في الآية المظلة أي الفلك

rows.speaker: المشهور
rows.claim: The familiar natural account says rising vapor forms cloud in cold air: moderate cold yields rain, stronger cold yields hail before vapor joins, and extreme cold can condense air into cloud and rain or snow; all remains governed by divine will and wisdom.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أن الابخرة إذا تصاعدت ولم تحللها حرارة فبلغت الطبقة الباردة من الهواء

rows.speaker: إخوان الصفاء
rows.claim: Ikhwan al-Safa explain that fine cloud differs from dense cloud; rain falls when water particles join, cool, and grow heavy, hail freezes after leaving cloud, and snow freezes within it.
rows.anchor: وفي "إخوان الصفاء" : الأجزاء المائية والترابية إذا كثرت في الهواء وتراكمت

rows.speaker: ابن التمجيد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Tamjid says sunlight on dry ground breaks off fiery particles that combine with earthy particles to form smoke.
rows.anchor: قال ابن التمجيد : إذا أشرقت الشمس على أرض يابسة تحللت منها أجزاء نارية

rows.speaker: شرح القانون
rows.claim: Sharh al-Qanun distinguishes smoke, made from earth and fire, from vapor, made from water and air; vapor is finer.
rows.anchor: وفي "شرح القانون" : الفرق بين الدخان والبخار هو أن تركيب الدخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs hail toward whom He wills, potentially harming people, crops, livestock, and fruit, and protects others from its danger.
rows.anchor: فيناله ما يناله من ضرر في نفسه وماله نحو الزرع والضرع والثمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنا with a short final vowel means bright light, while the extended form means height; lightning is the cloud's flash.
rows.anchor: فإن السنا مقصورا بمعنى الضوء الساطع وممدودا بمعنى الرفعة والعلو

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines lightning either as a flash of cloud or as an angel striking and moving the cloud so that fires appear.
rows.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : البرق واحد بروق السحاب أو ضرب ملك السحاب

rows.speaker: إخوان الصفاء
rows.claim: Ikhwan al-Safa describe lightning as fire sparked by friction among smoky particles inside the cloud.
rows.anchor: وفي "إخوان الصفاء" : البرق نار تنقدح من احتكاك تلك الأجزاء الدخانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightning nearly takes sight because of its extreme brightness and speed.
rows.anchor: يخطفها من فرط الإضاءة وسرعة ورودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because خلفة is a verbal noun, the construction needs an omitted noun; night and day succeed one another, allowing missed optional worship to be made up in the other period.
rows.anchor: مصدر للنوع فلا يصلح أن يكون مفعولا ثانيا لجعل

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet told Umar that a missed night recitation can be made up in daytime and a missed daytime recitation at night.
rows.anchor: وقد فاتته قراءة القرآن بالليل : "يا ابن الخطاب لقد أنزل الله تعالى فيك آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, night and day alternate so people can count years and time, and have set periods for earning a livelihood and for rest.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني جعلهما ذوي اعتقاب يجيء الليل ويذهب النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation recalls God's blessings and alerts people to His perfect wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: ففي الآية تذكير لنعمته وتنبيه على كمال حكمته وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering means reflecting on God's favors and creation to recognize the wise, necessary, merciful Creator; this is directed to unbelievers, while gratitude is directed to believers.
rows.anchor: أن يتذكر آلاء الله ويتفكر في صنعه فيعلم أن لا بد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شكورا with damma is a verbal noun for thanking God through obedience; أو may also mean and, making night and day occasions for remembering and thanking.
rows.anchor: بضم الشين مصدر بمعنى الشكر أي أن يشكر الله بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of أو emphasizes that either remembrance or gratitude independently fulfills the purpose; coordination with و might imply both are required together.
rows.anchor: ووجه التعبير بأو التنبيه على استقلال كل واحد منهما بكونه مطلوبا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines gratitude as recognizing and showing a favor, contrasts it with concealing blessings, and describes gratitude of heart, tongue, and limbs.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الراغب : الشكر تصور النعمة وإظهارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An optional litany is not legally obligatory to make up, but doing so is recommended: regular litany brings regular spiritual influx and connection, like a river supplied by mountain rain and snow.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن دوام الورد سبب لدوام الوارد ودوام الوارد سبب للوصلة

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: Sa'ib's couplet says a weak stream cannot reach the sea, illustrating why worshippers replace missed litanies to keep their spiritual supply flowing; the author urges morning and evening practice and warns against neglect.
rows.anchor: كما قال الصائب :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers came to their own peoples, as Muhammad came to his, each bringing proofs suited to prophethood.
rows.anchor: كما جئت قومك بالبراهين النيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals were punished for denying the prophets and persisting in denial; the relative clause marks the cause of punishment.
rows.anchor: فكذبوهم فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا من الجرم وهو تكذيب الأنبياء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say victory for believers is incumbent on God by generosity, not by an obligation imposed on Him.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : واجبا وجوب كرم لا وجوب إلزام

rows.speaker: الوسيط
rows.claim: Al-Wasit says God made victory incumbent upon Himself.
rows.anchor: وفي "الوسيط" : واجبا وجوبا هو أوجبه على نفسه

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says this resembles someone saying an undertaking is upon him, meaning he will do it.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : هذا كما يقال علي قصد هذا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory means saving believers from enemies and punishment; the wording honors them by presenting their rescue as a due claim upon God.
rows.anchor: وإنجاؤهم من شر أعدائهم وما أصابهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A hadith says that defending another Muslim's reputation obliges God to defend the defender from Hell; the Prophet then recites this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ما من امرىء مسلم يرد عن عرض أخيه إلا كان حقا

rows.speaker: أبو علي الروذباري
rows.claim: A story says Abu Ali served an ill poor disciple himself after others tired of caring for him; after death the man said he would support Abu Ali at Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: حكي عن الشيخ أبي علي الروذباري قدس سره : أنه ورد عليه جماعة من الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story teaches that God's beloved remain truly alive after death, moving from one abode to another.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن أحباب الله أحياء في الحقيقة وإن ماتوا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report urges giving kindness to the poor before their fortunes rise; on Judgment Day those helped with food, drink, clothing, or defense from slander will bring their benefactors into Paradise.
rows.anchor: والثاني : ما أشار إليه النبي عليه السلام بقوله : "اتخذوا الأيادي عند الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession belongs to the category of divine support and victory.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أن الشفاعة من باب النصرة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse promises the Prophet eventual triumph over deniers and tells believers that the outcome is theirs because they are mindful of God.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تبشير للنبي عليه السلام بالظفر في العاقبة والنصر على ما كذبه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In an inward reading, earlier messengers are spiritual masters appointed to train disciples; their proofs are verified teachings that guide sincere seekers to realization, while deniers remain distant.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" قوله : {ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم} يشير به إلى المتقدمين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading interprets God's victory for believers as His drawing near to those who draw near to Him.
rows.anchor: المتقربين إلينا بأن ننصرهم بتقربنا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds are winds of mercy, such as the east wind; إثارة means scattering clouds and raising them, and clouds is a generic noun usable for one or many.
rows.anchor: رياح الرحمة كالصبا ونحوها {فتثير سحابا}

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat derives clouds from dragging, either because wind drags them or because they carry water.
rows.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : أصل السحب الجر ومنه السحاب إما لجر الريح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds spread and dislodge clouds from their places; the action is attributed to the winds as its cause although God is the true agent.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فتنشره تلك الرياح وتزعجه وتخرجه من أماكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spreads the clouds as one connected mass in whichever direction and speed He wills, or separates them into pieces; كسفا is plural of a cloud fragment.
rows.anchor: يعني يجعله متصلا تارة {فى السمآء}

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says الودق may mean dust-like material within rain and may also denote rain itself; الخلل means a gap and جمعه is خلال.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الخلل فرجة بين الشيئين وجمعه خلال نحو خلل الدار والسحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain emerges by divine command from the cloud's holes and openings both when it is joined and when divided.
rows.anchor: فرج السحاب وشقوقه في التارتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are likened to a sieve so that rain does not damage the earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : السحاب كالغربال ولولا ذلك لأفسد المطر الأرض

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb reports that during the Flood the earth complained that unmeasured water had scratched and gouged it; God promised to make the clouds a sieve for rain.
rows.anchor: روي عن وهب بن منبه أن الأرض شكت إلى الله عز وجل أيام الطوفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God sends rain to chosen servants, they immediately rejoice at fertility and the end of drought; the pronoun refers to rain.
rows.anchor: الباء للتعدية والضمير للودق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers described are like the dead because their faculties are closed to truth; God knew before creating them that they would not believe.
rows.anchor: والكفار في التشبيه كالموتى لانسداد مشاعرهم عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that living people may be called dead when they gain no benefit from life; Ali says hoarders are dead while alive and scholars' effects remain after their bodies disappear.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أن الأحياء قد يسمون أمواتا إذا لم يكن لهم منفعة الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief is death of the heart and cancels hearing, while sin is illness that weakens hearing and requires treatment until it recovers.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الكفر موت القلب كما أن العصيان مرضه فمن مات قلبه بالكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deafness figuratively describes those who refuse to attend to truth; turning away makes their refusal complete, since someone facing the speaker might infer speech from gestures.
rows.anchor: والصمم فقدان حاسة السمع وبه شبه من لا يصغي إلى الحق ولا يقبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording underscores two joined faults: their ears reject truth and they deliberately turn away from hearing it.
rows.anchor: لبيان كمال سوء حال الكفرة والتنبيه على أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding Persian couplet urges people to return to their origin and seek spiritual hearing before the senses close and life's foundation collapses.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يرجع إلى أصله من صحبة الفروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, الله is the subject and الذي خلقكم is its predicate; خلقكم means He brought human beings into existence.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره قوله : {الذي خلقكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first weakness is the weak origin, semen or soil, with the verbal noun interpreted as an active noun; weakness is the opposite of strength.
rows.anchor: أي : من أصل ضعيف هو النطفة أو التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings differ: fatha is Tamim's dialect and the choice of Asim and Hamza in all three places; damma is Quraysh's dialect and the choice of other readers. Ibn Umar recited fatha and the Prophet read damma.
rows.anchor: والضعف بالفتح والضم خلاف القوة وفرقوا بأن الفتح لغة تميم واختاره عاصم وحمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second weakness is in the fetus and child; strength first appears in movement, seeking milk, and crying to repel harm.
rows.anchor: آخر وهو الضعف الموجود في الجنين والطفل

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars distinguish inner strength of cognition, strength experienced in the limbs, and later ability expressed in grasping and handling.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء أول ما يوجد في الباطن حول ثم ما يجربه في الأعضاء قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After puberty comes youthful strength, then old-age weakness and gray hair; repeated indefinites indicate distinct life stages rather than the same stage repeated.
rows.anchor: آخر هو ضعف الشيخوخة والكبر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib's grammatical rule, followed by major exegetes, is that repeating an indefinite noun refers to a different instance; he applies it to two eases following one hardship.
rows.anchor: هكذا حققه الإمام الراغب وتبعه أجلاء المفسرين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: An inward reading makes the stages weak reason, reason strengthened by proofs, then weakened faith when desire, illusion, and imagination distort inquiry into doubts that lead one from the straight path.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" {خلقكم من ضعف} في البداية وهو ضعف العقل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading warns that many who study speculative sciences to extinguish the light of the Law instead fall into the darkness of nature and seek to extinguish God's light.
rows.anchor: فيهلك كما هلك كثير ممن شرع في تعلم المعقولات لإطفاء نور الشريعة
